# Raincloud plots {#sec-raincloud-plots}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
# fonts ----
library(extrafont)
library(sysfonts)
source("_common.R")
# use font
showtext::showtext_auto()
# set theme
ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_rzone(
    base_size = 15))
library(raincloudplots)
library(ggdist)
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Theme: `theme_rzone()`

Graphs in this chapter use `fmggp2::theme_rzone()`, built from the Tiger R-Zone headset (1995): black plastic, a red frame and title, red LCD, purple logo, and pink marks, a pale blue visor text color, and an Arial Narrow title.
:::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}

<br>

```{r}
#| label: full_code_display
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '60%'
#| out-width: '60%'
#| fig-align: right
library(raincloudplots)
library(ggdist)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
set.seed(1994)
rzone_games <- tibble(
  player_id = 1:240,
  game = rep(c("Racing", "Fighting", "Shooter"), each = 80)) |>
  mutate(game = factor(game,
           levels = c("Racing", "Fighting", "Shooter")),
         seconds = round(rlnorm(n(), sdlog = 0.5,
           meanlog = log(c(Racing = 15, Fighting = 30,
                           Shooter = 60)[as.character(game)])), 1))
labs_raincloud_2 <- ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Tiger R-Zone",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    x = "Seconds to clear the first level",
    y = "Game")
ggplot(rzone_games,
    aes(x = seconds, y = game)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = game),
    notch = TRUE,
    notchwidth = 0.9,
    width = .15,
    outlier.shape = NA) +
  ggdist::stat_halfeye(aes(fill = game),
    adjust = 0.6, # shape = adjust * density estimator
    .width = 0, # can use probabilities or 0
    point_colour = NA, # removes the point in center
    orientation = "horizontal", # like the box plot
    height = 0.5, # height of curve
    justification = -0.3) + # shift vertically above box
    geom_point(aes(fill = game),
        shape = 21,
        color = "#ffffff",
        alpha = 1/3, size = 1.8,
    position = position_jitter(
      seed = 321,
      width = 0,
      height = .07)) +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    labs_raincloud_2
```

```{r}
#| label: full_code_raincloudplots
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '60%'
#| out-width: '60%'
#| fig-align: right
set.seed(1993)
rzone_tries <- faux::rnorm_multi(n = 100,
    mu = c(log(40), log(20)), sd = 0.5, r = 0.7,
    varnames = c("log_first", "log_second")) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(player_id = 1:100,
         first_try = round(exp(log_first), 1),
         second_try = round(exp(log_second), 1)) |>
  select(player_id, first_try, second_try)
rzone_1x1 <- raincloudplots::data_1x1(
  array_1 = rzone_tries$first_try,
  array_2 = rzone_tries$second_try,
  jit_distance = 0.2, # distance between points
  jit_seed = 2736) # used in set.seed()
ggp2_raincloud <- raincloud_1x1_repmes(
    data_1x1 = rzone_1x1,
    colors = (c('#FF2E93', '#14D8C4')),
    fills = (c('#FF2E93', '#14D8C4')),
    line_color = "#F2F0FF",
    line_alpha = 0.3,
    size = 0.8,
    alpha = 3/4
)
ggp2_raincloud_x <- ggp2_raincloud +
    scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = c(1, 2),
        labels = c("First try", "Second try"),
        limits = c(0, 3))
ggp2_raincloud_x +
    labs(title = "Tiger R-Zone",
        caption = "Simulated data",
        subtitle = "100 players, two tries each",
         x = NULL, y = "Seconds to clear the first level")
```

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"}
**Requirements:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a categorical variable**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a numeric (continuous) variable**
:::

::::

## Description

A raincloud plot shows where numbers fall in three ways at once.[^raincloud] The cloud is a line that is high where many numbers fall and low where few do, like a [density plot](density_plots.qmd). The box is a [box plot](box_plots.qmd). The rain is one point for each number, moved a little to the side so the points don't all fall on top of each other.[^rain] We can put rainclouds next to each other to compare where the numbers fall in each group.[^groups]

We can make raincloud plots with the [`raincloudplots` code](https://github.com/jorvlan/raincloudplots),[^pkg] or build them with the [`ggdist` code](https://mjskay.github.io/ggdist/) and the `geom_*()` parts of `ggplot2`.[^geoms]

## Set up

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**PACKAGES:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.95rem;"}
Bring in the code we'll use.[^packages]
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: pkg_code_raincloud
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide
remotes::install_github('jorvlan/raincloudplots')
remotes::install_github('mjskay/ggdist')
install.packages("faux")
library(raincloudplots)
library(ggdist)
library(faux) # for rnorm_multi()
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DATA:**
:::

Tiger's [R-Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R-Zone) (1995) was a game you wore on your head.[^console] A small card you put into it[^cartridge] showed the game in red, close in front of one eye.[^visor] The games were simple, so most players got through the first level much faster on their second try (if their eyes held out). We'll make up[^simulate] how many seconds it took 100 players to get through the first level on their first and second tries.

A log scale puts 0.1, 1, and 10 at even steps, so it shows how many times bigger one number is than another.[^log] A hill is a line that is high in the middle and low on both sides. `faux::rnorm_multi()` picks two columns of numbers from a hill, and the two columns go up and down together:[^mvn] the log of the first try (with its middle at 40 seconds) and the log of the second try (with its middle at 20 seconds). `r` sets how much the two tries move together (0.7),[^cor] so players who take a long time the first time often take a long time the second time too. `exp()` turns the logs back into seconds. Starting with `set.seed()`[^seed] means you'll get the same 100 players every time you run the code below.

`data_1x1()` from `raincloudplots` builds the data (`rzone_1x1`) for a graph of one group at two times, like the same players on two tries.[^repeated] We give it two lists of numbers (`array_1` and `array_2`),[^arrays] which we make from the `first_try` and `second_try` columns. `jit_distance` and `jit_seed` are for the points in the graph.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_code_raincloud
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
set.seed(1993) # same 100 players every time the code runs
rzone_tries <- faux::rnorm_multi(n = 100, # 100 different players
    mu = c(log(40), log(20)), # first try averages 40 seconds, second try 20 (on the log scale)
    sd = 0.5, # spread on the log scale
    r = 0.7, # players who are slow the first time are slow the second time
    varnames = c("log_first", "log_second")) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    player_id = 1:100, # one row per player
    first_try = round(exp(log_first), 1), # back to seconds
    second_try = round(exp(log_second), 1) # back to seconds
    ) |>
  select(player_id, first_try, second_try)
rzone_1x1 <- raincloudplots::data_1x1(
  array_1 = rzone_tries$first_try, # first group of points
  array_2 = rzone_tries$second_try, # second group of points
  jit_distance = 0.2, # distance between points
  jit_seed = 2736) # used in set.seed()
glimpse(rzone_1x1)
```
:::

## Distribution

A raincloud plot shows where all the numbers fall in three ways at once (the cloud, the box, and the rain).[^whole] The R-Zone data adds something new: the two groups are the *same* 100 players, each with two tries, so each first try goes with a second try from the same player.[^paired] Comparing the two clouds only tells part of the story; the two tries from each player tell the rest. Below we'll move from the players, to a graph, to the rule behind it.[^formula]

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**COUNT IT:**
:::

Start with the first five players.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_values_raincloud
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
head(rzone_tries, 5)
```
:::

Four of these five players got through the level much faster on their second try, but player 3 took more than two times as long. The numbers below compare the two tries for all 100 players.[^summary] The median is the middle number when you put all the numbers in order. The median drops by about half, almost every player was faster the second time, and `correlation` shows that long first tries go with long second tries.[^cor-summary]

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_summary_raincloud
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
rzone_tries |>
  summarise(median_first = median(first_try),
            median_second = median(second_try),
            share_faster = mean(second_try < first_try),
            correlation = cor(log(first_try), log(second_try)))
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DRAW IT:**
:::

The graph below puts each player's first try on the `x` axis and second try on the `y` axis, both on log scales. The line with no breaks in it[^solid] is "no change" (second try = first try), and the line made of short marks[^dashed] is "two times as fast" (second try = half the first try). The points come together around the line made of short marks, and they fall along a band instead of a round cloud because the two tries move together.[^band]

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: draw_raincloud
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
guide_lines <- tibble(
  line = c("No change", "Two times as fast"),
  intercept = c(0, log10(0.5)))
ggplot(rzone_tries, aes(x = first_try, y = second_try)) +
  geom_abline(data = guide_lines,
    aes(slope = 1, intercept = intercept, color = line, linetype = line)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, fill = "#FF2E93", color = "#ffffff",
    size = 2.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#F2F0FF", "#14D8C4")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "dashed")) +
  labs(x = "First try (seconds, log10 scale)",
       y = "Second try (seconds, log10 scale)",
       color = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**NAME IT:**
:::

The logs of the two tries come from [a hill with two numbers that move together](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multivariate_normal_distribution),[^bvn] which makes each try in seconds come from [a hill on the log scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log-normal_distribution):[^lognormal]

$$
\begin{pmatrix} \log(\text{first}) \\ \log(\text{second}) \end{pmatrix} \sim \text{Normal}\left(\begin{pmatrix} \log 40 \\ \log 20 \end{pmatrix}, \; \sigma = 0.5, \; \rho = 0.7\right)
$$

The difference between the two logs is the log of how much faster the second try was, $\log(\text{second} / \text{first})$.[^speedup] Its middle is at $\log(20 / 40) = \log(0.5)$ (two times as fast), and how far it usually falls from that middle is $\sigma\sqrt{2(1 - \rho)} = 0.5\sqrt{0.6} \approx 0.39$.[^sd] Because the two tries move together, that number gets smaller: if the two tries had nothing to do with each other ($\rho = 0$),[^independent] it would be $0.5\sqrt{2} \approx 0.71$, and many more players would have taken longer the second time. That's why data with two tries from each player[^paired-data] (and raincloud plots that join each player's two tries with a line) can show a difference that we can't see in two clouds on their own. Try changing `r` to `0` in `rnorm_multi()`, and the band of points opens up into a cloud.


## Grammar (`raincloudplots`)

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**CODE:**
:::

Make the words around the graph[^labels] with `labs()`

Build the graph with `raincloudplots::raincloud_1x1_repmes()`, and give `rzone_1x1` to `data_1x1`

  - set `colors` and `fills`

  - set `line_color` and `line_alpha` for the lines that join each player's two tries

  - set the `size` of the points and `alpha` (how much we can see through them)[^alpha]

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_raincloud
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
ggp2_raincloud <- raincloudplots::raincloud_1x1_repmes(
    data_1x1 = rzone_1x1,
    colors = (c('#FF2E93', '#14D8C4')),
    fills = (c('#FF2E93', '#14D8C4')),
    line_color = "#F2F0FF",
    line_alpha = 0.3,
    size = 0.8,
    alpha = 3/4)
ggp2_raincloud_x <- ggp2_raincloud +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = c(1, 2),
        labels = c("First try", "Second try"),
        limits = c(0, 3))
ggp2_raincloud_x +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Tiger R-Zone",
        caption = "Simulated data",
        subtitle = "100 players, two tries each",
        x = NULL,
        y = "Seconds to clear the first level")
```
:::



::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**GRAPH:**
:::

```{r}
#| label: create_graph_raincloud
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
ggp2_raincloud <- raincloudplots::raincloud_1x1_repmes(
    data_1x1 = rzone_1x1,
    colors = (c('#FF2E93', '#14D8C4')),
    fills = (c('#FF2E93', '#14D8C4')),
    line_color = "#F2F0FF",
    line_alpha = 0.3,
    size = 0.8,
    alpha = 3/4)
ggp2_raincloud_x <- ggp2_raincloud +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = c(1, 2),
        labels = c("First try", "Second try"),
        limits = c(0, 3))
ggp2_raincloud_x +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Tiger R-Zone",
        caption = "Simulated data",
        subtitle = "100 players, two tries each",
         x = NULL,
        y = "Seconds to clear the first level")
```

## More info

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DATA:**
:::

We'll make up first tries for 80 players on each of three kinds of R-Zone games (`rzone_games`). Each kind of game gets its own middle time (15, 30, or 60 seconds),[^typical] and `rlnorm()` picks each player's time from a hill on the log scale.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_code_ggdist
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
set.seed(1994) # same 240 players every time the code runs
rzone_games <- tibble(
  player_id = 1:240, # 240 different players, one row each
  game = rep(c("Racing", "Fighting", "Shooter"), each = 80) # 80 players per game
  ) |>
  mutate(
    game = factor(game,
      levels = c("Racing", "Fighting", "Shooter")), # shortest to longest
    seconds = round(
      rlnorm(n(), sdlog = 0.5, # seconds to finish the first level (skewed right)
        meanlog = log(c(Racing = 15, Fighting = 30, # typical seconds
                        Shooter = 60)[as.character(game)])), # (looked up for each game)
      1 # one decimal place
      )
    )
glimpse(rzone_games)
```
:::

### Box-plot

  -   Make the words around the graph with `labs()`

  -   Start the graph with `ggplot()` and give it `data`

  -   For the first part of the graph,[^layer] make a box plot with `geom_boxplot()`, but make each box less wide around the median[^notch] and don't show the points for numbers that are far from the rest.[^outliers] The part that is less wide shows about where the median would fall if we could see every player of that game.[^notch-ci] The rain we add below still shows the far points.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: create_graph_raincloud2_box
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
labs_raincloud_2 <- ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Tiger R-Zone",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    x = "Seconds to clear the first level",
    y = "Game")
ggp2_box <- ggplot(rzone_games,
    aes(x = seconds, y = game)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = game),
    notch = TRUE,
    notchwidth = 0.9,
    width = 0.15,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    show.legend = FALSE)
ggp2_box +
    labs_raincloud_2
```
:::

### Density

Next we add the cloud with `ggdist::stat_halfeye()`, so it runs along the `x` axis like the box.[^halfeye] We give each `game` its own color with `fill`, change how big the cloud is and its form,[^adjust] and move it a little above the box plot.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: create_graph_raincloud2_halfeye
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
ggp2_stat_halfeye <- ggp2_box +
  ggdist::stat_halfeye(aes(fill = game),
    adjust = 0.6, # shape = adjust * density estimator
    .width = 0, # can use probabilities or 0
    point_colour = NA, # removes the point in center
    orientation = "horizontal", # like the box plot
    height = 0.5, # height of curve
    justification = -0.3, # shift vertically above box
    show.legend = FALSE # don't need this
)
ggp2_stat_halfeye +
    labs_raincloud_2
```
:::

### Points

The last part of the graph is `geom_point()`.[^last-layer] We give each `game` its own color with `fill`, and set `position` to `position_jitter()`.[^jitter] We also change the points in two more ways:

- With `shape = 21`, we can `color` the outside of each point (white makes it look like it gives off light).

- Set the `height` by hand, which is how far up and down the points can move, and set `width = 0` so each point stays at its number of seconds. The points move up and down a little so they don't cover each other.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: create_graph_raincloud2_jitter
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
ggp2_jitter <- ggp2_stat_halfeye +
    geom_point(aes(fill = game),
        position = position_jitter(
          seed = 321,
          width = 0,
          height = .07),
            shape = 21,
            color = "#ffffff",
            alpha = 1/3,
            size = 1.8,
            show.legend = FALSE)
ggp2_jitter +
    labs_raincloud_2
```
:::

## More examples & resources

### Point shape

Cédric Scherer makes graphs and writes about how to make them. #TidyTuesday puts out a new set of data each week for people to make graphs with. Cédric wrote about raincloud plots in [this great piece](https://www.cedricscherer.com/2021/06/06/visualizing-distributions-with-raincloud-plots-and-how-to-create-them-with-ggplot2/) for [#TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday).

Cédric also shows other ways to put the points in the graph (I really like using bands instead of points when the rainclouds stand up and down).[^bands]

We can change to this form by adding `ggplot2::coord_flip()` to `ggp2_stat_halfeye`, which turns the graph on its side,[^flip] then adding `geom_point()` with `shape` set to `95`

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: create_graph_raincloud2_point_lines
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
ggp2_stat_halfeye +
    ggplot2::coord_flip() +
ggplot2::geom_point(
    shape = 95,
    size = 8,
    alpha = 0.2) +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    labs_raincloud_2
```
:::

[^raincloud]: A combination of a density graph (the cloud), a box plot (the box), and a beeswarm or jitter plot (the rain).

[^rain]: The points are jittered.

[^groups]: Compare the distributions of a numeric variable across the levels of a categorical (or discrete) grouping variable.

[^pkg]: The `raincloudplots` package.

[^geoms]: The `ggdist` package and geoms from `ggplot2`.

[^packages]: Install and load the packages.

[^console]: A game console.

[^cartridge]: A cartridge.

[^visor]: The cartridge projected red LCD graphics onto a small visor.

[^simulate]: Simulate.

[^log]: A logarithmic (log) scale.

[^mvn]: `faux::rnorm_multi()` draws two correlated columns from a normal distribution.

[^cor]: The correlation (`r`).

[^seed]: Setting the random seed.

[^repeated]: A 1x1 repeated measures graph.

[^arrays]: Two array arguments.

[^whole]: A whole distribution.

[^paired]: The two groups are the same 100 players measured twice, so each first try has a partner (paired) second try.

[^formula]: The formula.

[^summary]: The summary.

[^cor-summary]: The correlation of the log times.

[^solid]: The solid line.

[^dashed]: The dashed line.

[^band]: Because of the correlation.

[^bvn]: A bivariate normal distribution.

[^lognormal]: Each try is log normal on the seconds scale.

[^speedup]: The log of the speed up.

[^sd]: The standard deviation of the log difference.

[^independent]: Independent.

[^paired-data]: Paired data.

[^labels]: Labels.

[^alpha]: `alpha` sets opacity.

[^typical]: A typical (median) time.

[^layer]: The first layer.

[^notch]: Notches.

[^outliers]: Hide the outliers in the box plot layer (`outlier.shape = NA`). The jittered points added later still draw them.

[^notch-ci]: The notch is roughly a 95% confidence interval around the median. If the notches of two boxes don't overlap, their medians likely differ.

[^halfeye]: A horizontal density curve.

[^adjust]: The size (`height`) and shape (`adjust`) of the density curve.

[^last-layer]: The final layer.

[^jitter]: `position_jitter()` moves each point a small random distance so the points don't cover each other.

[^bands]: Bands are short lines (`shape = 95`) in place of points, shown when the rainclouds are vertical.

[^flip]: `coord_flip()` swaps the `x` and `y` axes, so the rainclouds are vertical.

[^gist]: A GitHub gist.
